## Generalize additive models

@secor2025 provided a simple generalized additive model (GAM) evaluated in R [@r_2026] for the analysis of marine fauna flyways. In the manuscript, the average latitude per individual, per week of a Hudson River population of striped bass _Morone saxatilis_, possibly the entire population of North Atlantic right whale _Eubalaena glacialis_, and several populations of northern gannet _Morus bassanus_ were regressed against date. We reproduce that analysis here for an expanded data set of striped bass locations which includes Potomac and Delaware populations (["Initial striped bass GAM exploration"](striped_bass_gam.qmd)) as well as for tagged sand tiger sharks _Carcharias taurus_ (["Initial striped bass GAM exploration"](sand_tiger_gam.qmd)). An initial analysis of Atlantic sturgeon _Acipenser oxyrinchus_ is ongoing.

## Functional data analysis

Flyway models can viewed as a form of functional data analysis (FDA, see @gertheiss2024 for a current review), where the observation unit is a "function" rather than a single point. In many ways, FDA can be viewed as a further generalization of generalized additive models. While we do not plan to pursue this further, an initial exploration is provided in [the Functional Data Regression chapter](fda.qmd).
